claims.text: Wear resistance in HEA protective coatings is primarily governed by dynamic stabilization of a dense nanocrystalline grain-boundary network.
A dense nanocrystalline grain-boundary network facilitates strain-induced self-hardening during sliding wear.
Increasing grain size through mild pre-annealing will reduce dynamic hardening.
Reduced dynamic hardening caused by grain coarsening will lower wear performance.
The initial coatings have a nanocrystalline, multiphase microstructure optimized for wear resistance.
Mild pre-annealing can be used to systematically increase average grain size.
High mixing entropy stabilizes a fine-grained HEA microstructure.
The fine-grained microstructure impedes dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion enables strain-induced self-hardening during wear.
Pre-annealing increases average grain size and reduces grain-boundary density.
Reduced grain-boundary density diminishes the coating's ability to immobilize dislocations under load.
A diminished ability to immobilize dislocations reduces dynamic self-hardening.
Pre-annealed, coarser-grained samples will exhibit less dynamic hardening than as-deposited, finer-grained samples during sliding wear.
Pre-annealed, coarser-grained samples will have higher wear rates than as-deposited, finer-grained samples.
The proposed mechanism should govern sliding wear from room temperature to approximately 200°C.
Outside the stated temperature regime, other wear mechanisms such as tribo-oxidation may become dominant.
The quantitative relationship between grain-size increase and loss of wear resistance is uncertain.
